title: Checkpoint: Baroque and Classical
objective: After this level you can compare Baroque and Classical music.
summary: Baroque music (about 1600 to 1750) wove intricate polyphony over a continuo; the Classical style of Haydn and Mozart made one clear melody the norm, with simplicity and clarity.

cards.headline: Chapter 4 finale: when music changed its texture.
cards.body: Bach died in 1750, and the Baroque era is usually said to end about then. What came next, the Classical style that Haydn and Mozart brought to its height in Vienna, didn't just add new forms. It changed how the lines of music fit together. Here are the two eras side by side.

cards.headline: Baroque and Classical, side by side

items.label: Classical, the later 1700s
points: One clear melody leading the way
No continuo; the orchestra's four sections
The string quartet as chamber music's star

cards.headline: The big switch: from many lines to one tune
cards.body: The deepest change was texture. Late Baroque music loved intricate polyphony, several lines woven together, like the voices entering a fugue. Classical composers reacted against it: a texture dominated by melody became the norm, one clear tune on top with the other parts supporting it, and forms were built for simplicity and clarity. Level 1's melody moved into the spotlight.

mascot.line: Baroque: everyone talks at once, brilliantly. Classical: one speaker, and everyone else nods along.

cards.headline: What stayed, what changed hands
cards.body: Some things were handed down and remade. The continuo was abandoned after about 1770, and the orchestra settled into Mannheim's four sections. The Baroque opera overture grew into the Classical symphony. Every level in this chapter is one piece of that handover.

cards.headline: Chapter 4 complete
learned: How Baroque music's woven lines over a continuo bass gave way to the Classical style's one clear tune.
How a fugue passes one theme from voice to voice, and why Bach's fame needed a revival.
Where opera came from, and how recitative and aria split the job of telling a story.
Why the orchestra settled into four sections and came to need a conductor out front.

questions.prompt: Reacting against late-Baroque polyphony, what texture did Classical composers make the norm?

options.label: Dense polyphony, like a fugue
options.rationale: That is what they reacted against.

options.label: Melody-led homophony, one tune on top
A bass line with figured chords
options.rationale: That is the Baroque continuo, which faded.

questions.explanation: Classical composers made a texture dominated by melody the norm, built for simplicity and clarity.

questions.prompt: A harpsichord improvises chords over a bass line while several tunes weave in imitation. Which era fits best?

options.label: The Classical era
options.rationale: Classical music dropped the continuo and favored one clear melody.

options.label: Neither: it describes a string quartet
options.rationale: A string quartet has no harpsichord.

questions.explanation: A continuo and interwoven polyphony are Baroque hallmarks.

questions.prompt: From Level 33: what did the sonnets printed with Vivaldi's Four Seasons do?

options.label: Gave the words the soloist sings
options.rationale: The Four Seasons is purely instrumental.

options.label: Described the scenes the music paints
Listed the tempo in beats per minute
options.rationale: They are poems, not tempo markings.

options.label: Dedicated the work to Haydn
options.rationale: Mozart's quartets were dedicated to Haydn.

questions.explanation: Each sonnet describes scenes, and letters show where the music depicts them: program music.

questions.prompt: From Level 35's timeline: which is the first opera whose music survives complete?

options.label: Peri's La Dafne (1598)
options.rationale: Probably the first opera, but not the one that survives complete.

options.label: Monteverdi's Orfeo (1607)
options.rationale: Orfeo is the first to stay in the repertory, but it came later.

options.label: Handel's Messiah (1742)
options.rationale: Messiah is an oratorio, and much later.

questions.explanation: Peri's L'Euridice of 1600 is the first opera whose music survives complete.

questions.prompt: From Level 37: what did the Classical symphony grow out of?

options.label: The string quartet
options.rationale: The quartet is chamber music; the symphony came from opera.

options.label: The Baroque fugue
options.rationale: The fugue is a technique, not the symphony's ancestor.

options.label: The Mannheim crescendo
options.rationale: That was an orchestral effect, not a form.

questions.explanation: The symphony grew from the Italian opera overture, the fast-slow-fast sinfonia.
